Multi-protocol

Serve HTTP, TCP, WebSocket, QUIC, gRPC and other protocols in one Go application. KPro provides component assembly, message routing and lifecycle management.

Protocol handlers

Use native HTTP and gRPC handlers

HTTP and gRPC keep their own handler interfaces. Message protocols such as TCP and WebSocket share Message / Context and message routing. One server manages startup, readiness and shutdown for all mounted components.

Service structure

Connect your handlers to one server

Create a server, mount the protocol components you need, and register handlers and routes. The diagram shows how the application, shared runtime and protocol components fit together.

01

Startup and shutdown

Validate configuration and wait for components to become ready. During shutdown, close components in order and wait for outbound queues to drain within the configured timeout.

02

Queues and concurrency

Configure Router queue capacity and in-flight limits, plus message-count and byte limits for transport outbound queues.

03

Application responsibilities

Implement authentication, authorization, business idempotency and delivery requirements in your application. Configure and validate deployment capacity for your workload.

v0

Version and usage

KPro is currently pre-1.0

The current release includes configuration validation, resource limits, shutdown handling and observability support, with repository tests and benchmark budget checks. APIs are not frozen. Before deployment, validate your protocol combination, workload and deployment environment.
